overview: WiseTech Global is an Australian-founded, engineer-led developer of CargoWise, a deeply integrated global software platform that lets logistics service providers, freight forwarders and 3PLs run complex, multi-country logistics transactions on one database. The company serves more than 20,000 logistics companies across 193 countries, including 24 of the top 25 global freight forwarders and 47 of the top 50 global 3PLs, and after completing the US$2.1bn acquisition of e2open in August 2025 has expanded into supply-chain orchestration, taking its network to over 500,000 connected enterprises. WiseTech reported in AUD through FY2024 and switched its functional/reporting currency to USD from H1 FY2025 onward, reflecting its increasingly US-weighted revenue base post-e2open.

business_model.summary: Revenue is overwhelmingly recurring: customers pay for CargoWise principally through cloud-delivered, usage-based licensing (Recurring On-Demand License revenue) plus subscription/maintenance fees, with a small non-recurring tail of one-time license and professional-services/support revenue. Growth comes from a mix of new CargoWise customer wins (notably Large Global Freight Forwarder, or LGFF, rollouts), rising transaction usage and price increases among an extremely sticky existing base (customer attrition on the core CargoWise suite has been under 1% for 14+ years), and acquisitions of logistics/supply-chain software companies that are cross-sold into the installed base. A new commercial model, CargoWise Value Packs (CVP), launched December 2025, is being rolled out across the customer base and is intended to simplify pricing and lift adoption. The August 2025 e2open acquisition materially changed the mix, adding a sales-led, professional-services-heavier, lower-margin subscription business that management is transitioning toward WiseTech's product-led model.

revenue_streams.name: Recurring Subscription and One-Time License (OTL) Maintenance revenue (mostly e2open subscription)
OTL and support/professional services
revenue_streams.trend: growing (e2open-driven), declining as % of revenue as services shift to WiseTech Partner Network

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — global freight forwarders, third-party logistics providers (3PLs), customs brokers, and post-e2open, manufacturers/retailers/distributors doing supply-chain orchestration
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations across 193 countries with main data centers/delivery hubs in Australia, Europe and the U.S.; product development centers span 40 countries including centers of excellence in Sydney, Bengaluru and Nanjing; e2open acquisition further increased US revenue and cost-base weighting, consistent with the FY2025 switch to USD reporting

competitive_position.market_position: Estimated global leader in freight-forwarder logistics execution software with roughly 20-22% share by some industry estimates; entrenched with 24 of the top 25 global freight forwarders and 47 of the top 50 global 3PLs on CargoWise; e2open adds a leadership position in supply-chain orchestration per Gartner, IDC and Nucleus Research rankings

moat_factors.description: CargoWise is mission-critical, deeply configured software run on a single global database across multiple offices, currencies and regulatory regimes; migrating a large global freight forwarder is a multi-year, high-risk undertaking, evidenced by sub-1% annual attrition sustained for 14+ years

A multi-sided marketplace connecting carriers, forwarders, importers, exporters and shippers becomes more valuable as more counterparties are onboarded; e2open's 500,000+ connected enterprises extend this network into manufacturing and distribution

Cumulative product investment exceeding $1.1bn over FY22-FY26 and 6,500+ product enhancements create a functionality gap smaller vendors struggle to match, particularly in complex cross-border compliance

Reputation among the largest global freight forwarders creates a credible reference base for further large-account wins (61 LGFF rollouts secured as of FY26, with the majority of contracted volume not yet live, implying built-in future revenue)
Deep compliance capability across customs, trade and border regimes in 193 countries is costly to replicate and valuable to enterprise customers navigating tariff/trade complexity

weaknesses: Founder-dependency and recent governance instability created uncertainty around strategic continuity

e2open brings a structurally lower-margin, professional-services-heavy, sales-led business that is diluting group gross margin (FY26 group gross margin fell to 77% from 86% in FY25) and has been suffering subscription revenue attrition during integration
Large, debt-funded M&A (e2open) raises integration execution risk and financial leverage that the pre-2025 organic-growth, net-cash WiseTech did not carry

Competitors like Descartes and DSV are reported to be probing CargoWise pricing/lock-in dynamics amid the CVP commercial model transition, creating some customer-relationship risk during the changeover
Now under active ACCC investigation for alleged Competition and Consumer Act contraventions, adding regulatory and reputational overhang

growth_drivers: Continued Large Global Freight Forwarder (LGFF) rollouts — 61 secured as of FY26 with more than 75% of contracted volume for in-progress rollouts not yet live, representing built-in future revenue

CargoWise Value Packs (CVP) commercial model, adopted by 95%+ of CargoWise customers, with new SME signings up ~55% year-on-year, intended to simplify pricing and drive higher usage-based monetization

CargoWise AI and broader AI Transformation program — six AI agents live, targeting up to ~50% labor-cost savings for logistics customers, plus internal AI-driven productivity gains (annualized EBITDA run-rate savings of $34m from the FY26 Product & Development/Customer Service program, on top of $17m from an earlier program)

e2open integration and cross-sell — expands the network into connected supply-chain orchestration across manufacturing, channels and distribution; already delivered annualized run-rate cost synergies of $64m in FY26, surpassing the original FY27 target of $50m, with 8pp of e2open Underlying EBITDA margin expansion versus FY25 pro forma

Expansion into adjacent markets beyond core CargoWise logistics: TradeWise (trade finance/banking), customs and government, and VerifyWise (verified identity/trust and data), building toward the stated vision of an 'operating system for global trade and logistics'

Continued bolt-on M&A of logistics/supply-chain software vendors in target geographies and technology adjacencies (e.g., FRDM.ai supply-chain risk/compliance intelligence acquisition completed August 2026)
Container Transport Optimization (CTO) platform, which went live July 2026, building on Matchbox Exchange and Avantida to expand a network of container transport participants

business.description: Richard White remains Executive Director and Chief Innovation Officer after stepping down as Executive Chair in July 2026; the company explicitly flags succession planning around its Founder as a key risk, and cultural/strategic continuity depends heavily on retaining senior leadership post-turmoil

Company explicitly identifies integration of large acquisitions, particularly e2open, as resource-intensive with risk that expected benefits/ROI are not fully realized; e2open experienced continued subscription revenue attrition during FY26 as integration and commercial-model transition progressed

Company cites risk that pace and complexity of concurrent initiatives (e2open integration, CVP commercial model evolution, AI-enabled development, adjacent-market expansion) stretch resources or introduce technical/execution challenges

Migration of legacy STL (subscription/term-license) customers to the new CVP model created some 2H26 revenue refinements; competitors reportedly probing pricing and lock-in dynamics during the changeover window
Company itself flags risk from competitor product innovation, price discounting, in-house systems preference by some logistics providers, and new cloud-based entrants

financial.description: Total debt rose from ~$65m at FY25 to ~$2,187m at FY26 (and $2,362m at H1 FY26) to fund the fully debt-financed e2open acquisition; net finance costs jumped from $3.5m in FY25 to $131.7m in FY26; interest rate swaps have been used to hedge a portion of the exposure

Net tangible asset backing was negative $2,117.0m (FY26) versus negative $103.3m (FY25), reflecting substantial goodwill/intangibles from e2open; not itself a solvency issue given $1.1bn+ total liquidity, but signals the scale of M&A-driven balance sheet transformation

Revenue is invoiced and costs incurred across many currencies; the FY2025 switch from AUD to USD reporting reflects growing USD exposure; FX hedging is used but translation and transaction effects still move reported results

financial.risk: Margin dilution from acquired business mix
financial.description: e2open's higher professional-services mix and headcount-heavy cost of revenue structurally lowers e2open's own gross margin, diluting group gross margin (77% FY26 vs 86% FY25; 85% ex-e2open)

regulatory.description: On 19 August 2026 the ACCC executed a search warrant and commenced an investigation into an alleged contravention of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010; no specific provisions or findings have been disclosed publicly; shares fell roughly 10-13% on the news. This follows a January 2026 ACCC-accepted court-enforceable undertaking requiring divestment of e2open's Expedient business as an acquisition condition
Growth (organic and acquisitive) increases exposure to a wide range of compliance and regulatory requirements across many jurisdictions; company monitors but cannot eliminate this exposure

FY25 board review into Executive Chair Richard White's conduct found he had misled the board about personal relationships; he blocked release of the report before an independent chair (Raelene Murphy) was appointed in July 2026 — residual governance/reputational risk despite resolution steps taken

macro.risk: Global trade and industrial production volumes
macro.description: FY27 guidance is explicitly conditioned on market conditions and current supply-chain volume trends not materially changing; management flags that changes in industrial production and/or global trade (tariffs, trade wars, demand shifts), both favorable and unfavorable, could move guidance

As software embedded in global freight/customs execution, WiseTech's usage-based CargoWise revenue is correlated with global trade and shipping volumes, which are sensitive to tariffs and geopolitical trade tensions
The debt taken on for e2open increases sensitivity to interest rates despite partial hedging via interest rate swaps

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global freight-forwarding and supply-chain software market is expanding as logistics providers digitize and adopt cloud-based, compliance-heavy platforms; WiseTech's own estimate is ~20-22% share of the freight-forwarder software market with room to grow via LGFF rollouts and adjacent-market expansion (trade finance, customs/government, identity/trust)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — usage-based CargoWise revenue correlates with global trade/shipping transaction volumes, but the very high (95%+ in FY26) recurring revenue base and sub-1% attrition provide meaningful downside protection versus a purely cyclical logistics operator
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Elevated versus history following the debt-funded e2open acquisition; net finance costs rose from $3.5m (FY25) to $131.7m (FY26); partially hedged via interest rate swaps

recent_developments.event: FY26 results: revenue up 79% to $1,395.9m driven by e2open consolidation and CargoWise growth; statutory NPAT down 11% to $178.7m on higher finance costs and restructuring; underlying NPAT up 29% to $313.5m; FY27 guidance of $1.48-1.54bn revenue (6-10% growth) and $725-780m underlying EBITDA (12-21% growth, 49-51% margin) issued alongside leadership updates; shares fell ~10% on the guidance/updates
ACCC executed a search warrant at WiseTech and commenced an investigation into an alleged contravention of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010; shares fell 10-13% on the news
Completed acquisition of FRDM.ai (AI-powered supply-chain risk and compliance intelligence) for ~$24.3m total consideration, net of cash acquired — not material to the Group but strategically aligned

Richard White stepped down as Chair (remaining Executive Director and Chief Innovation Officer); Raelene Murphy appointed Independent Chair of the Board, completing a governance reset that began with the February 2025 board resignations

1H FY26 results: revenue up 76% to $672.0m; operating profit flat at $149.6m; statutory NPAT down 36% to $68.1m; underlying NPAT up 2% to $114.5m; company reaffirmed FY26 guidance and highlighted accelerating AI Transformation savings
ACCC accepted a court-enforceable undertaking requiring WiseTech to divest e2open's Expedient business as a condition tied to the e2open acquisition
Launched CargoWise Value Packs (CVP), a new commercial/pricing model now adopted by more than 95% of CargoWise customers; drove ~55% YoY growth in new SME signings

Completed the US$2.1bn enterprise value, fully debt-funded, public-to-private acquisition of e2open (at $3.30/share cash), materially expanding WiseTech's network to 500,000+ connected enterprises and shifting reporting currency emphasis toward USD
WiseTech appointed Zubin Appoo as Chief Executive Officer as part of the post-governance-crisis leadership reset

Four of six WiseTech directors (Chairman Richard Dammery, Lisa Brock, Fiona Pak-Poy, Michael Malone) resigned amid 'intractable differences' over Richard White's position, following a board review that found White had misled the board about personal relationships
Richard White stepped down as CEO after allegations about his personal conduct surfaced, remaining as Executive Chair at the time

items.notes: Represents 6-10% YoY growth off the FY26 base of $1,395.9m; growth guidance is a sharp moderation from FY26's 79% (largely e2open-driven) as that acquisition anniversaries
Represents 12-21% growth and an Underlying EBITDA margin of 49-51%, implying continued material margin expansion versus FY26 (FY26 underlying EBITDA was $644.5m)

items.target: Assumes no material change in market conditions
items.notes: Management explicitly flagged that changes in industrial production and/or global trade volumes (favorable or unfavorable) could move actual results outside the guided range

items.target: Achieved $64m annualized run-rate savings in FY26
items.period: FY26 actual, exceeding original FY27 target
items.notes: Original synergy target was $50m by FY27; WiseTech reported surpassing this in FY26 already, with 8pp of e2open Underlying EBITDA margin expansion versus FY25 pro forma

guidance.management_commentary: Management said the FY27 guidance range reflects views on customer adoption of the new CVP commercial model, further delivery and adoption of agentic AI within CargoWise, and the launch/adoption of new products including VerifyWise — with the lower end of guidance assuming growth broadly in line with FY26 and modest adoption of new initiatives, and the upper end assuming accelerated adoption. Despite record FY26 revenue and underlying NPAT, shares fell roughly 10% on the results day, reflecting investor concern about the moderating growth outlook, leadership changes (new independent chair, new Audit and Risk Committee chair), and the newly disclosed ACCC investigation landing in the same reporting window.

bull_case: Extremely sticky, high-margin core CargoWise business with sub-1% customer attrition sustained for 14+ years and 95%+ recurring revenue, giving strong visibility and pricing power

Large embedded revenue pipeline from LGFF rollouts already contracted but not yet live (more than 75% of contracted volume for in-progress rollouts as of FY26), representing built-in multi-year growth independent of new sales

e2open integration is ahead of plan on cost synergies ($64m annualized run-rate achieved in FY26 versus a $50m FY27 target), with clear margin-expansion trajectory (49-51% FY27 EBITDA margin guidance) as the deal is digested

Governance reset now largely complete — independent chair appointed, new CEO in place since July 2025, new Audit and Risk Committee chair — removing much of the overhang that depressed sentiment through FY25/early FY26

AI-driven productivity gains (internal engineering and customer service efficiency, plus CargoWise AI agents targeting ~50% labor cost savings for customers) provide a structural margin and product-differentiation lever few smaller competitors can match given WiseTech's R&D scale
bear_case: FY27 guidance of only 6-10% revenue growth, sharply below FY26's e2open-inflated 79%, disappointed the market and shares fell roughly 10% on results day, suggesting the market is questioning underlying organic momentum once the e2open base effect fades

Active ACCC investigation (search warrant executed August 2026) into alleged Competition and Consumer Act contraventions creates open-ended regulatory, legal cost and reputational risk, on top of an earlier forced Expedient divestment tied to e2open approval

Debt-funded e2open acquisition transformed the balance sheet from net cash to ~$2.2bn of debt and negative $2.1bn NTA, with finance costs surging to $131.7m in FY26 from $3.5m in FY25 — integration missteps or a rate environment shift would be more costly than in WiseTech's pre-2025 history

e2open itself is a structurally lower-margin, services-heavy business still experiencing subscription revenue attrition during its transition to WiseTech's product-led model, diluting group gross margin from 86% to 77% and adding execution risk on top of the CVP commercial-model transition for legacy CargoWise customers

Founder/key-person risk remains explicitly flagged by the company itself — Richard White stepped back from Chair but remains Executive Director and Chief Innovation Officer after a governance crisis (2024 CEO departure amid personal conduct allegations, four director resignations in Feb 2025, a board report he blocked from release) — full resolution of cultural and strategic continuity risk is not yet proven
